content:
alex: heads up — after yesterday's routing policy bump we see p95 for /v1/generate diverging between endpoint-level and merged rollup dashboards. p50 matches but p95/p99 are ~20-30ms different :confused:

maria: saw that too. can you paste sample counts? rolled up view shows ~120k samples, endpoint shows 18k for the same time window.

alex: here's quick query I ran: `select sum(count) as total, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) from metrics where route='/v1/generate' group by endpoint` — totals differ by ~x6. suspect routing weights causing duplicate attribution or weighted samples.
devon: my hunch: t-digest rollups + weighted sampling from router are getting merged incorrectly. t-digest merge expects raw samples or counts but not "weighted entries" we added for routing shuffle.
maria: can you show the exact merge call? we use td.merge(other) in aggregator.
devon: code snippet:
```
# simplified
a = TDigest(compression=100)
a.update_from_histogram(hist)  # we store hist-ish blobs
b = TDigest(...)
a.merge(b)
# if b was produced from weighted sampling (weight != 1), the weight was encoded in `count` field but our exporter dropped the metadata
```

jen: we changed the router to add `sample_weight` tag when rerouting on fallback. the telemetry export pipeline flattens tags -> we probably lost it. ops-bot showed the routing deploy at 1747000000 in case it's relevant.

samir: confirming: when we fallback route, we set weight=route_multiplier so the aggregator can compute correct per-endpoint quantiles. if weight gets dropped, td.merge thinks all samples equal and merged digest skews.
maria: that would explain p50 unaffected (robust) but tails shift. p95/p99 are sensitive to weighting. nice catch.

alex: quick repro idea: create two small tdigests with overlapping tails and merge with and without weights and compare approx_percentile outputs. can someone run a quick test in staging?
devon: I'll spin up a small notebook. quick command to pull stored blobs: `curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/v1/blobs?route=/v1/generate&ts=1747110000" | jq .`

jen: short-term mitigation: tag the rollup UI with "sampling source: merged" and add sample counts visible next to percentiles so SREs notice regression. also add a note on the rollout that router introduced weighted sampling flag.
maria: long-term: exporter should preserve `sample_weight` and aggregator must support weighted tdigest merge or instead merge histograms + counts then convert to tdigest. proposal: change pipeline to store histograms + counts as the canonical rollup proto.
samir: +1. Also can we add an automatic sanity check: if route rollup count != sum(endpoint counts) by >10% flag the rollup as "inconsistent" in console?
devon: implementation note: weighted tdigest isn't in our current lib. alternative: expand kafka schema to include a `weight` field and alter aggregator to expand weighted samples into repeated samples when weight < some threshold (ugly) or use reservoir sampling with weight support.

alex: action items:
- devon: quick repro & post numbers (ETA 2h)
- jen: add sample_count next to percentiles in dashboard (ETA EOD)
- maria: open exporter PR to preserve sample_weight (ETA tomorrow)
- samir: design alert for inconsistent counts (ETA two working days)

jen: noted. I'll mock the UI change with a tooltip: "counts may diverge when routing uses weighted sampling" so support teams aren't confused.

maria: small PSA for rollouts channel: please avoid enabling weighted sampling until exporter+aggregator support it. cc @rollouts.

ops-bot: deployment: router-v2 rolled out to prod at 2024-06-09T02:00:00Z (build 5f3a2c) :shipit:

alex: thanks all. will sync after devon posts repro. :thumbsup:
